subject: Mathematics
title: Permutations and Combinations
summary: Counting starts with the fundamental principle: if one job can be done in m ways and another in n ways, both together can be done in m × n ways (and either one in m + n ways).
Permutations count arrangements (order matters): ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!. Combinations count selections (order doesn't matter): ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!).
Special cases: identical objects, circular arrangements, restrictions (together / never together), distribution of identical objects (stars and bars) and derangements.

formulas.name: Fundamental principle
formulas.when: Breaking a counting problem into stages.

formulas.name: Permutations
formulas.formula: ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!;  with repetition allowed: nʳ

formulas.name: Combinations
formulas.formula: ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!);  ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ;  ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ
formulas.note: If ⁿCₓ = ⁿCᵧ then x = y or x + y = n.

formulas.name: Identical objects
formulas.formula: n!/(p! q! r! …) for p alike of one kind, q of another, …

formulas.name: Together / never together
formulas.formula: k particular objects together: treat as one block → (n − k + 1)! × k!;  never together = total − together

formulas.name: Gap method
formulas.formula: to keep k objects apart, arrange the others first, then choose gaps: (n − k)! × ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁺¹Pₖ

formulas.name: Distributing identical objects
formulas.formula: n identical objects into r groups: ⁿ⁺ʳ⁻¹Cᵣ₋₁ (empty allowed);  ⁿ⁻¹Cᵣ₋₁ (each group ≥ 1)
formulas.when: Stars and bars / non-negative integer solutions of x₁ + … + xᵣ = n.

formulas.name: Derangements
formulas.when: No object in its own place.

formulas.name: Selections from identical objects
formulas.formula: from p alike, q alike, r alike: (p + 1)(q + 1)(r + 1) − 1 non-empty selections;  from n distinct: 2ⁿ − 1

formulas.name: Geometry counting
formulas.formula: lines through n points (no 3 collinear) = ⁿC₂;  triangles = ⁿC₃;  diagonals of n-gon = ⁿC₂ − n;  with m collinear: subtract ᵐC₂ − 1 lines, ᵐC₃ triangles

formulas.name: Number of divisors
formulas.formula: if N = p^a q^b r^c then divisors = (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1);  sum of divisors = Π (p^{a+1} − 1)/(p − 1)

examples.title: Round table
examples.problem: In how many ways can 6 people sit at a round table? And 6 beads on a necklace?

examples.title: Committee
examples.problem: Choose 3 men from 5 and 2 women from 4.

examples.title: Derangements of 4 letters
examples.problem: In how many ways can 4 letters go into 4 addressed envelopes with none in the right one?

examples.title: 4-digit numbers
examples.problem: How many 4-digit numbers can be formed from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
examples.solution: First digit: 5 choices (not 0); remaining 3 places from 5 digits: ⁵P₃ = 60. Total = 5 × 60 = 300.

examples.title: Identical balls
examples.problem: In how many ways can 10 identical balls go into 3 different boxes (empty allowed)?

examples.title: Diagonals
examples.problem: How many diagonals does a decagon have?

topics.title: Factorial basics
topics.explain: n! = n(n − 1)…1; 0! = 1. ⁿPᵣ = r! × ⁿCᵣ. The exponent of a prime p in n! is [n/p] + [n/p²] + [n/p³] + … (e.g. number of trailing zeros in 100! is 24).

topics.title: Words with restrictions
topics.explain: Vowels together: treat vowels as one block. Vowels at odd places: choose places for vowels first. Dictionary (rank) problems: count words starting with each smaller letter in turn.

topics.title: Grouping and division
topics.explain: Dividing m + n distinct objects into two groups of m and n: (m + n)!/(m! n!). Into groups of equal size (unlabelled), divide also by the factorial of the number of equal groups.

topics.title: Circular with restrictions
topics.explain: Two particular people together at a round table: (n − 2)! × 2!. Men and women alternating (n each): (n − 1)! × n!.

topics.title: Integer solutions
topics.explain: Number of positive integral solutions of x + y + z = 10 is ⁹C₂ = 36; non-negative solutions are ¹²C₂ = 66. For upper limits, use inclusion–exclusion or coefficients of polynomial expansions.

topics.title: When order matters
topics.explain: Ask 'does swapping two chosen items give a new outcome?' — if yes, permutation; if no, combination. Most errors come from counting a selection as an arrangement.

ratta: ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!;  ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!).
